title: Born in Chicago
description: Samuel Harris Altman is born in Chicago, Illinois, the eldest of four children of dermatologist Connie Gibstine and Jerold (Jerry) Altman in a Reform Jewish family.
notes: Birth time is not recorded on any certificate in the dossier; the only source is Altman's Dec 6 2023 email to astrologer Jessica Josephine saying 'around 5 am central time' (Astro-Databank Rodden A, from memory). Chicago was on CST (UTC-6); DST began Apr 28 1985.

title: Infancy in Chicago (quiet period)
description: First years of life in Chicago before the family's move to Missouri; no dated events are documented for this stretch.
notes: Quiet stretch; dossier has no dated events.

title: Early technical precocity
description: In nursery school he grasps the system behind telephone area codes; a later feature says he fixed the family VCR at about age three.
notes: Area-code anecdote is Altman's own account (New Yorker 2016); VCR story is single-source color. v1 places nursery school in St. Louis (~1988-1991), v2 says late 1980s.

title: Family moves to Clayton, Missouri
description: The family relocates from Chicago to Clayton, a St. Louis suburb and his father's hometown, when Sam is about four; he grows up in the Hillcrest area near Forest Park.
notes: Year 1989 rests on one Wikipedia citation chain; v2 also gives ~1988-1989. 'Born in St. Louis' variants are errors.

title: Childhood in Clayton (quiet period)
description: Ordinary childhood years in a two-career household (dermatologist mother, real-estate broker father) with three younger siblings, described as competitive across games, puzzles, sport and school.
notes: Few dated events; household color is from a single 2025 feature (WashU Common Reader).

title: First computer at eighth birthday
description: Receives a Macintosh LC II for his 8th birthday; learns to program and take hardware apart, later calling it a 'dividing line in my life' and a lifeline to the world.
notes: Model is Macintosh (LC II per v1), not Apple II.

title: Youngest sibling Ann born
description: His sister Ann (Annie), the youngest of the four children, is born; the sibling set is Sam, Max, Jack and Annie.
notes: Year derived: the complaint pleads her age as 30 at the Jan 2025 filing and age 3 in ~1997. Max's and Jack's birth years are not in the dossier.

title: AOL chat rooms while privately gay
description: At about 11-12 he finds AOL chat rooms 'transformative' while privately working out that he is gay; he later says growing up gay in the Midwest 'was not the most awesome thing'.

title: Attends John Burroughs School
description: Attends John Burroughs School, an elite St. Louis prep school; mentored by CS teacher Georgeann Kepchar (early AI talks), edits the yearbook, plays water polo, builds the school website, does Model UN.
notes: Start year not documented ('late 1990s'); teacher Abbott details are REPORTED via BI summary of Bloomberg.

title: School assembly coming-out speech
description: After students boycott or skip a school assembly about sexuality, he addresses the whole student body, says he is gay, and asks whether the school wants to be repressive or open; a counsellor later says 'What Sam did changed the school.'
notes: Trigger wording varies by source (Christian-group boycott vs no-show vs National Coming Out Day speaker); v1 dates ~2001-2003, v2 ~2001-2002.

title: Comes out to his parents
description: At about 16 he tells his parents he is gay; his mother says she was 'astonished' because he had struck her as 'unisexual and tech-y'.

title: Graduates high school
description: Graduates from John Burroughs School with the Class of 2003.
notes: Spring 2003; month approximate.

title: Enters Stanford, moves to California
description: Enrolls at Stanford University to study computer science (reportedly working in the AI lab), leaving Missouri for California.
notes: Fall 2003; AI-lab detail is REPORTED.

title: Stanford years (quiet period)
description: Two undergraduate years in computer science; he plays a lot of poker and later recommends it as training in decision-making.
notes: Few dated events.

title: Relationship with Nick Sivo begins
description: Begins a relationship with classmate Nick Sivo, later his Loopt co-founder; it lasts about nine years ('I thought I was going to marry him').
notes: Start year conflict: v1 says sophomore year 2004-2005; v2 gives ~2003-2012. Start is inferred, not stated by Altman.

title: Drops out of Stanford at 19
description: Leaves Stanford after two years, without a degree, to work on Loopt full time.
notes: v1 grades REPORTED, v2 VERIFIED. Month uncertain: v2 says spring 2005; v1 notes he had 'just finished sophomore year' during YC summer 2005.

title: Overwork gives him scurvy
description: Works so incessantly during the Loopt build summer that he develops scurvy, by his own later account.
notes: His own anecdote via New Yorker 2016.

title: Loopt in Y Combinator's first batch
description: Loopt (first called Radiate) is funded in YC's inaugural Summer Founders batch in Cambridge, MA ($6k per founder) alongside Reddit; start of his relationship with Paul Graham and YC.

title: Loopt raises Series A
description: Loopt raises about $5M from Sequoia and NEA.
notes: v2 dates the round Nov 2005; v1 records it disclosed at the Sep 2006 launch.

title: Joins Twitter as @sama
description: Opens the @sama account (user ID 1605), later his main public channel.
notes: Corrects a common 2007-08 assumption.

title: Loopt launches publicly
description: Loopt launches on Boost Mobile; at 21 he is a press-profiled CEO ('21-year-old CEO'), with about 40,000 subscribers by November.
notes: Launch time differs by ~1 hour across source metadata (vB); evening Sep 11 PT.

title: Graham calls him 'Bill Gates at 19'
description: Paul Graham's essay names Loopt the most promising of his first batch and compares the young Altman to Bill Gates at 19.

title: Loopt Series B and Sprint deal
description: Loopt raises a Series B (reported $8.25M) and wins carrier distribution with Sprint.
notes: Round size disputed ($8.25M vs $12M authorized).

title: Demos Loopt at Apple WWDC keynote
description: Demonstrates Loopt on stage at Steve Jobs' WWDC keynote; Graham writes that he got there by being 'extremely effective'.

title: Loopt iPhone launch and SMS-invite backlash
description: Loopt for iPhone ships with the App Store; the app mass-texts users' address books and ignores STOP replies, drawing backlash, apologies and a fix a week later.

title: Graham's 'king of the cannibals' line
description: In 'A Fundraising Survival Guide' Graham writes that if Altman were parachuted onto an island of cannibals he would be king within five years.
notes: Quote is Graham's (Aug 2008), not Thiel's.

title: Loopt sued for patent infringement
description: Earthcomber sues Loopt for patent infringement; the suit is dropped in March 2009.

title: Loopt explores a sale in the financial crisis
description: During the 2008 financial crisis Loopt hires Allen & Co. to explore financing or a sale.

title: Named among Graham's five founders
description: Graham names the 24-year-old Altman one of the five most interesting founders, writing 'On questions of strategy or ambition I ask, What would Sama do?'.

title: Loopt pivots: Mix, GraffitiGeo, Pulse
description: Loopt spins out its Mix dating feature, buys YC-backed GraffitiGeo and launches Pulse local search, chasing a new product direction.

title: Begins angel investing
description: Starts making angel investments (later 100+ companies, including Stripe and Airbnb-era bets), the base of his later personal wealth.
notes: Company names are reported; check dates are not.

title: Loopt plateau (slow period)
description: Loopt has about 4M users and 45 staff and ships updates but cannot find growth; years of grind before the sale.

title: Facebook Places undercuts Loopt
description: Facebook launches Places; Loopt's position collapses and Steve Boom becomes Loopt president while Altman stays CEO.
notes: Date VERIFIED; competitive impact REPORTED.

title: Becomes part-time YC partner
description: Joins Y Combinator as a part-time partner while still running Loopt, alongside Garry Tan, Emmett Shear and Justin Kan.
notes: v1 REPORTED (roster not re-verified, vB #63); v2 VERIFIED.

title: Nine-year relationship ends
description: He and Nick Sivo break up after the Loopt sale, ending a nine-year relationship.

title: Loopt sold to Green Dot
description: Green Dot agrees to buy Loopt for $43.4M cash (incl. ~$9.8M retention); a negative return for VCs, but his first liquidity (he kept about $5M).
notes: SEC URL fails (vB #57); terms corroborated via TechCrunch. Closed ~end Mar/Apr 4 2012. 'Help save face' framing is REPORTED (2026).

title: Co-founds Hydrazine Capital with brother Jack
description: Starts Hydrazine Capital with his brother Jack: a $21M fund mostly from Peter Thiel, with much of his own Loopt proceeds, investing heavily in YC companies.
notes: Month from Wikipedia only; year confirmed across aggregators.

title: Post-Loopt interregnum (quiet period)
description: Low-profile stretch: a post-close role at Green Dot (Loopt tech feeds GoBank), Hydrazine investing and part-time YC work, while Graham courts him as successor.
notes: Few dated events.

title: Graham first approaches him to run YC
description: Paul Graham first raises the idea of Altman succeeding him as head of YC; the courtship lasts over a year.
notes: 'Mid-2012'; month approximate.

title: Named president of Y Combinator
description: Graham announces Altman, 28, as YC president from the next batch: 'YC needs to get bigger, and I am not really much of a manager. Sam Altman is.'
notes: Date confirmed; YC-blog clock time UNVERIFIABLE (vA, vB).

title: First big YC reform: the 'New Deal'
description: On his 29th birthday he announces YC's standard $120k-for-7% deal, his first major policy as president.
notes: YC blog body UNVERIFIABLE in vB; terms via TechCrunch.

title: Teaches Stanford's 'How to Start a Startup'
description: Co-teaches Stanford CS183B, putting YC's curriculum (and himself) in front of a mass audience.

title: Leads Reddit's $50M Series B
description: Personally leads Reddit's $50M round (~$500M valuation) and later joins its board; ends up a ~9% pre-IPO holder.
notes: v1 dates Oct 2014 (month); v2 Sep 30 2014 (TC).

title: Eight days as Reddit interim CEO
description: After Yishan Wong resigns, he serves as Reddit's interim CEO for about eight days and installs Ellen Pao as interim CEO.
notes: He preceded Pao (inverted framing corrected in v1).

title: Becomes Helion investor and chairman
description: Becomes investor and chairman of fusion company Helion Energy (later also chairs fission startup Oklo).
notes: Oklo chair start date not in dossier.

title: Meets Oliver Mulherin
description: Reportedly meets his future husband, Australian software engineer Oliver Mulherin, late at night in Peter Thiel's hot tub.
notes: From Keach Hagey's book via secondary sources; book text not retrieved. A 2026 New Yorker snippet says they met nine years earlier.

title: Turns 30; 'days are long' essay
description: Shortly after turning 30 he publishes 'The days are long but the decades are short', a list of life lessons.

title: Pitches Musk a 'Manhattan Project for AI'
description: Emails Elon Musk proposing a YC-led 'Manhattan Project for AI'; Musk replies it is 'probably worth a conversation', the seed of OpenAI.
notes: Exhibit known via The Verge's trial exhibit log; vB downgrades Verge-log rows to REPORTED and could not re-page Ex.3.

title: OpenAI founding dinner
description: Brokers the Rosewood Sand Hill dinner with Musk, Sutskever and Brockman that starts OpenAI's recruitment.

title: Expands YC: Research, Continuity, Fellowship
description: Launches nonprofit YC Research with $10M of his own money, plus the YC Fellowship (Jul 2015) and the ~$700M Continuity growth fund (Oct 2015).
notes: Continuity fund size REPORTED.

title: Co-founds OpenAI
description: OpenAI is announced as a nonprofit with ~$1B pledged; Altman and Musk are co-chairs, while he remains YC president.

title: Launches basic-income pilot
description: Announces YC's unconditional basic-income pilot in Oakland, later his personally funded OpenResearch study.
notes: Research request posted Jan 27 2016.

title: President of YC Group; Seibel runs core
description: Michael Seibel becomes CEO of YC's core program while Altman, now president of YC Group, focuses on expansion and OpenAI.

title: YC Group era (steady period)
description: Steady expansion of YC under his presidency: Startup School MOOC (2017), batches growing to 124 then 200+ companies, YC China (Aug 2018), while OpenAI takes more of his time.

title: New Yorker 'Manifest Destiny' profile
description: Tad Friend's New Yorker profile fixes his public image: childhood, coming out, Graham's 'extremely good at becoming powerful', and a prepper inventory that spreads as a 'survivalist' story.

title: Prepper posture made public
description: Says he keeps 'guns, gold, potassium iodide, antibiotics, batteries, water, gas masks' and land in Big Sur he can fly to, with a fallback plan to fly to Thiel's New Zealand house; also races cars (two McLarens) and flies rented planes.
notes: Big Sur parcel never identified; no later restatement of prepping found. Mother adds he 'keeps an awful lot tied up inside' and has 'cyber-chondria'.

title: Publishes 'The Merge'
description: Essay arguing that the human-AI merge has already started and is probably the best-case scenario.

title: OpenAI control fight with Musk peaks
description: Musk demands majority equity and control of a for-profit OpenAI; Sutskever and Brockman refuse ('AGI dictatorship'), Musk writes 'Discussions are over', and Altman says he remains enthusiastic about the nonprofit.
notes: All exhibit rows downgraded from VERIFIED to REPORTED by vB (Verge-log transmission).

title: Musk leaves OpenAI board
description: Musk leaves the board (Tesla conflict cited) after the control fight and stops funding at about $100M of a ~$1B pledge; Altman takes on the president role, leaving OpenAI short of money.
notes: Departure VERIFIED; motives and pledge figures REPORTED; Musk's total giving is contested ($38M-$45M+).

title: OpenAI Charter published
description: OpenAI publishes its Charter on broadly distributed benefits, safety and leadership.

title: Father dies
description: His father, Jerold Donald (Jerry) Altman (b. Oct 4 1950), dies at 67; memorial May 28 at Central Reform Congregation, St. Louis.
notes: Full name and dates per vA correction. Cause of death not established (heart-attack claim quarantined). A 2023 NY Mag profile calls it a tipping point for his sister's mental health.

title: Co-founds Tools for Humanity / Worldcoin
description: Co-founds iris-scanning identity and crypto project Worldcoin (Tools for Humanity) with Alex Blania; he is chairman.
notes: v1 lists 2019-10-21 at year precision.

title: 'How To Be Successful' essay
description: Publishes a 13-point manifesto on compounding and self-belief ('Compounding is magic').

title: Steps down as YC president
description: Steps down as YC president to become chairman as he moves to OpenAI.
notes: Exit framing contested: contemporaneous posts describe a mutual transition; post-2023 anonymous accounts and the 2026 New Yorker say he was pushed out over mistrust; Graham said in May 2024 he 'wasn't fired'.

title: Becomes OpenAI CEO; capped-profit LP
description: OpenAI creates a capped-profit LP (100x cap) under nonprofit control, with Altman as CEO; he takes no equity.

title: Leaves YC leadership
description: Geoff Ralston becomes YC president and Altman drops from chairman to adviser, ending his formal YC role.
notes: 'Chairman into 2021' is stale boilerplate (v1 conflict #9).

title: Pre-ChatGPT build years (lower-profile period)
description: Relatively quiet public years running OpenAI: GPT-3 and the API (2020), DALL-E and Copilot (2021), plus large personal property purchases during the pandemic.

title: Microsoft invests $1B
description: Microsoft invests $1B in OpenAI with an exclusive Azure partnership, securing compute.

title: Buys Napa ranch
description: Buys a 950-acre working ranch in Napa for $15.7M, later his weekend home with Mulherin.

title: Buys Russian Hill home in San Francisco
description: Buys a $27M Russian Hill compound (950 Lombard) via LLC, later his main San Francisco home.

title: Large Democratic political donation
description: Gives $250,000 to a pro-Biden super PAC, consistent with a Democratic donor record.

title: OpenAI's first commercial product
description: OpenAI opens the GPT-3 API, its first revenue product, under his CEO tenure.

title: Puts $180M into Retro Biosciences
description: Funds longevity startup Retro Biosciences' entire $180M seed; in 2023 says he put 'all my liquid net worth' into Helion and Retro.
notes: Date conflict: v1 says 2021 checks (revealed Mar 8 2023); v2 says Apr 2022.

title: 'Moore's Law for Everything'
description: Essay proposing an American Equity Fund taxing companies and land to pay every adult (illustrated at $13,500/yr).

title: Buys Hawaii estate
description: Buys a $43M Kailua-Kona estate on Hawaii's Big Island, the reported site of his 2024 wedding.
notes: Bedroom count conflict 12 (BI) vs 10 (Sotheby's).

title: Worldcoin unveiled
description: Worldcoin is publicly introduced (orb iris scans for a free token share), beginning years of privacy controversy.

title: $375M Helion check
description: Leads Helion's $500M Series E with about $375M of his own money, his biggest personal investment.
notes: Round VERIFIED; personal ticket REPORTED (CNBC).

title: Public family estrangement with sister begins
description: His sister Ann begins public social-media accusations against him (date per his later counterclaim); the family says she has been estranged and receiving support.
notes: Recorded only as start of public estrangement; content not repeated. Date is as alleged in Sam's Mar 2025 counterclaim (Doc 18).

title: Leaves Reddit board
description: Leaves Reddit's board, keeping a large stake ahead of its IPO.

title: ChatGPT launches
description: OpenAI releases ChatGPT; it reaches 1M users in five days and ~100M within two months, making him a global figure.
notes: Toner later says the board learned of the launch on Twitter (disputed).

title: Microsoft multibillion investment
description: Microsoft announces a multiyear, multibillion-dollar investment (reported ~$10B).
notes: $10B figure REPORTED only.

title: Musk turns publicly hostile
description: Musk attacks OpenAI as a 'closed maximum-profit' company; Altman texts him 'you're my hero' and that the attacks 'really fucking hurt'.
notes: Texts known via trial exhibits (REPORTED per vB).

title: 'Planning for AGI and Beyond'
description: Publishes OpenAI's AGI strategy, backing iterative deployment and admitting its original openness view was wrong.

title: GPT-4 launch
description: OpenAI launches GPT-4.

title: Testifies to the US Senate
description: Testifies before Senate Judiciary on AI oversight, calling for licensing and warning 'if this technology goes wrong, it can go quite wrong'; seen as the reasonable face of AI.

title: World tour with heads of state
description: Tours Europe, the Middle East and Asia meeting Sánchez, Macron, Sunak, Modi and others; an EU 'cease operating' remark draws rebuke and a walk-back, and an India 'hopeless' remark draws backlash.

title: Signs AI extinction-risk statement
description: Signs the CAIS statement that mitigating extinction risk from AI should be a global priority.

title: Public as a couple at White House dinner
description: Attends the White House state dinner for Narendra Modi with Oliver Mulherin, their first notable public appearance as a couple.

title: Worldcoin launch and regulatory backlash
description: Worldcoin's token and network launch; Kenya suspends it on Aug 2, starting a run of regulator actions across many countries.

title: Says he plans children soon
description: Tells New York Magazine that he and Mulherin plan to have kids soon; they live at the Napa ranch.

title: Board friction over Toner paper
description: Board member Helen Toner co-authors a paper that reportedly angers him; executives reportedly bring the board concerns about his conduct, and he reportedly moves to push Toner out.
notes: Exec complaints relayed by Toner; NYT account second-hand. Unadjudicated.

title: High school alumni award
description: Receives John Burroughs School's Outstanding Alum Award at an assembly.

title: First DevDay, peak before the fall
description: Hosts OpenAI's first DevDay (GPT-4 Turbo, GPTs); ChatGPT has 100M weekly users. Eleven days later he is fired.

title: Fired as OpenAI CEO
description: In a noon video call the board removes him as CEO and director, saying he was 'not consistently candid'; Murati becomes interim CEO and Brockman quits.
notes: Board post first archived 20:30:25 UTC. Directors reportedly decided ~Nov 11 (Hao, anonymous). Cause disputed: candor (board) vs safety (denied by WilmerHale) vs Q* (single anonymous Reuters claim, excluded). He was in a Las Vegas hotel room (his 2025 'Reflections').

title: Negotiating return over the weekend
description: Explores a new AI-chip venture while investors press the board; visits HQ with a guest badge and posts 'i love the openai team so much' (Nov 19), prompting mass staff echoes. His Russian Hill home serves as a war room.
notes: 'i love the openai team' is Nov 19 04:47 UTC, not Nov 22 (vB #45).

title: Microsoft offer and staff revolt
description: The board names Emmett Shear interim CEO; Nadella announces Altman will lead a new Microsoft AI team; most of ~770 staff sign a letter threatening to leave unless he returns, and Sutskever says he regrets his role.
notes: Signature counts are dated snapshots only (>500/700+ Axios; 738/~770 Wired; 'vast majority' Guardian); no frozen 745 roll (vA). Murati signed first.

title: Returns as OpenAI CEO
description: An agreement in principle (late Nov 21 PT / Nov 22 UTC) restores him as CEO under a new initial board (Taylor, Summers, D'Angelo) without a board seat; formalized Nov 29, with an independent review promised.
notes: Return date differs by time zone (Nov 21 PT vs Nov 22 UTC).

title: TIME CEO of the Year
description: Named TIME's 2023 CEO of the Year two weeks after his reinstatement.
notes: Same day he emailed an astrologer his birth time ('around 5 am central'), the only source for his birth time.

title: Independent review of firing begins
description: WilmerHale is retained to investigate the firing; UK and US regulators start examining the Microsoft-OpenAI tie.

title: New York Times sues OpenAI
description: The New York Times sues OpenAI and Microsoft for copyright infringement, the lead case in a wave of copyright suits.

title: Marries Oliver Mulherin
description: Marries Oliver Mulherin in a small seaside ceremony with about a dozen guests, reportedly at his Hawaii estate; photos surface and he confirms it Jan 10-11.
notes: Exact day and site unresolved: Jan 10 vs 11, or late 2023 (PinkNews); Hawaii estate vs 'undisclosed tropical beach'. NBC confirmation URL unverifiable (vA). He later called married life 'very happy'.

title: SEC probe reported
description: The SEC reportedly examines whether his communications misled investors.

title: Musk sues him and OpenAI
description: Musk sues OpenAI, Altman and Brockman in San Francisco for breaching the founding nonprofit mission; OpenAI answers by publishing Musk's old emails (Mar 5).
notes: v1 REPORTED, v2 VERIFIED (docket CGC-24-612746).

title: First LGBTQ media interview
description: In his first LGBTQ media interview (The Advocate) he talks about growing up gay and says married life feels 'different and better. I'm very happy.'

title: Review clears return; rejoins board
description: WilmerHale's review finds a breakdown in trust but that his conduct 'did not mandate removal'; he rejoins the board with three new directors.
notes: Only a company-published summary exists; full report never released (discount weight).

title: Concedes governance failure on Lex Fridman
description: On Lex Fridman's podcast he concedes that a board able to fire him but unable to make it stick is a governance failure, while defending his conduct.

title: GPT-4o, 'her' post and Johansson dispute
description: After the GPT-4o launch and his one-word 'her' post, Scarlett Johansson says the Sky voice is 'eerily similar' to hers after she declined twice; OpenAI pauses Sky (May 19) and he apologizes for poor communication.
notes: Imitation unadjudicated; no lawsuit found through Sep 2026 (absence REPORTED only).

title: Sutskever leaves OpenAI
description: Co-founder and chief scientist Ilya Sutskever, who voted to fire him, departs on warm public terms; Altman calls him 'a dear friend'.

title: Leike quits over safety culture
description: Safety lead Jan Leike resigns saying safety 'took a backseat to shiny products' and the Superalignment team is dissolved; Altman replies 'he's right we have a lot more to do'.

title: Signs the Giving Pledge with his husband
description: He and Mulherin sign the Giving Pledge, promising most of their wealth to 'technology that helps create abundance'; announced May 28.

title: Exit-NDA equity clawback scandal
description: He posts that OpenAI 'never clawed back' vested equity and he was unaware of the provision; leaked documents contradict that, he says he is embarrassed, and ex-staff are released from non-disparagement (May 23).

title: Toner's public account of the firing
description: Former director Helen Toner says on the TED AI Show that he withheld information, misrepresented things and 'in some cases outright' lied to the board; board chair Bret Taylor rebuts.
notes: VERIFIED that she said it; underlying claims are her account. Her Loopt/YC firing claims are single-source and quarantined. Date: May 28 PT / May 29 UTC (vA).

title: Graham: he wasn't fired from YC
description: Paul Graham publicly states Altman was not fired from YC; Taylor and Summers defend him in The Economist.
notes: v1 REPORTED; v2 VERIFIED direct quote via TechCrunch.

title: 'Right to Warn' letter
description: Current and former frontier-lab staff publish a letter demanding no gag NDAs and protection for safety critics.

title: Musk drops his state lawsuit
description: Musk voluntarily dismisses the California state suit; Apple announces ChatGPT integration the day before.

title: Sues over defective SF home
description: His Russian Hill compound is the subject of a 'lemon' construction-defect suit against builder Troon Pacific over leaks, sewage and mold (claimed repairs >$4M).

title: Basic-income study results
description: OpenResearch, funded by him, publishes first results of its 3-year, 3,000-person unconditional cash study.

title: Co-founder Schulman leaves; Brockman on leave
description: Co-founder John Schulman leaves for Anthropic and Greg Brockman takes extended leave through November.

title: Musk refiles in federal court
description: Musk revives his case as Musk v. Altman in federal court in Oakland, the case that goes to trial in 2026.
notes: v1: docket VERIFIED, date REPORTED.

title: 'The Intelligence Age'
description: Essay saying 'deep learning worked' and superintelligence may arrive in 'a few thousand days'.

title: Says psychedelics changed him
description: On a podcast he says a guided psychedelic weekend in Mexico turned him from a 'very anxious, unhappy person' into 'a very calm person'; he has chaired psychedelic-medicine startup Journey Colab.
notes: Date is the disclosure; the retreat's date is unknown. His words via Fortune/BI; audio not retrieved.

title: Murati and top researchers leave
description: CTO Mira Murati resigns, with research chief Bob McGrew and Barret Zoph, during the push to convert to a for-profit; he denies reports he would get 7% equity.
notes: Exits VERIFIED (Reuters); motive disputed; same-day McGrew/Zoph detail Wikipedia-sourced in v1.

title: Raises $6.6B at $157B
description: OpenAI closes a $6.6B round at a $157B valuation.

title: Joins SF mayor-elect's transition team
description: Named to San Francisco Mayor-elect Daniel Lurie's transition team.

title: Ex-OpenAI researcher dies
description: Former OpenAI researcher Suchir Balaji, a copyright critic, dies by suicide (no foul play per autopsy); conspiracy claims later follow Altman, including a Sep 2025 Tucker Carlson interview.
notes: Death VERIFIED; any claim of Altman involvement is NOISE and is not recorded as fact.

title: For-profit conversion plan
description: OpenAI proposes converting its business into a public benefit corporation, a saga that runs until the Oct 2025 restructuring.

title: $1M to Trump's inauguration
description: Pledges $1M to Donald Trump's inaugural fund, a break from his Democratic donor history.

title: Says he has not slept well since ChatGPT
description: Says he hasn't had a good night's sleep since ChatGPT launched; later says his routine 'fell to crap' after becoming a parent.
notes: Snippet-level sourcing; no exact date.

title: 'Reflections' essay; expecting a child
description: Writes that his firing was 'a big failure of governance by well-meaning people, myself included' and 'we know how to build AGI'; on a podcast he says they are expecting a child.
notes: Child-expectation remark REPORTED via BI.

title: Sister files lawsuit; family denies
description: His sister Ann Altman files a civil suit against him in federal court in St. Louis (E.D. Mo. 4:25-cv-00017). On Jan 7 he, his mother and brothers issue a joint statement calling the claims 'utterly untrue'.
notes: Recorded only as filed/denied/status; allegations not repeated. Press dates Jan 7-8 reflect publication lag; docket stamp is Jan 6.

title: Stargate at the White House
description: Announces the $500B Stargate AI-infrastructure venture with Trump, SoftBank's Son and Oracle's Ellison on Trump's second day; Musk publicly mocks it and they spar on X.
notes: v1 REPORTED, v2 VERIFIED (OpenAI/SoftBank posts).

title: DeepSeek shock
description: Chinese lab DeepSeek's cheap R1 model wipes out AI stocks; he calls it 'invigorating' and pulls releases forward.

title: Musk's $97.4B bid for the nonprofit
description: A Musk-led group offers $97.4B for OpenAI's nonprofit; the board rejects it Feb 14 ('not for sale'); a court later calls it a 'sham bid' per counterclaims.

title: Expands Russian Hill compound
description: An affiliate run by his cousin buys three adjacent Russian Hill lots.
notes: Price conflict: records $14M vs MLS ~$38M.

title: Son is born
description: Announces the birth of a son with Mulherin, born early and in the NICU: 'i have never felt such love.' The name is undisclosed.
notes: Post text known only via proxy (vA: REPORTED-proxy); v2 grades VERIFIED. Surrogacy reported by tertiary sources only (quarantined). Some outlets date it Feb 23-24 by time zone.

title: Judge denies Musk bid to block conversion
description: A federal judge denies Musk's request for a preliminary injunction against OpenAI's for-profit conversion.

title: Answers sister's suit with counterclaims
description: He files a denial plus counterclaims for abuse of process and defamation seeking $1 in nominal damages ('does not want to harm his sister financially') and moves to dismiss.

title: Raises $40B at $300B
description: OpenAI closes a $40B SoftBank-led round at $300B after a viral image-generation surge.

title: OpenAI countersues Musk
description: OpenAI countersues Musk for a bad-faith campaign to slow it down; in April he also steps down as Oklo chairman to avoid conflicts.

title: Musk suit trimmed
description: Judge Gonzalez Rogers dismisses part of Musk's claims (false advertising, fiduciary duty) while fraud and unjust-enrichment claims continue toward trial.

title: Retreats: nonprofit keeps control
description: Under pressure from critics and attorneys general, OpenAI says its nonprofit will keep control.

title: Critical biographies published
description: Karen Hao's book (excerpted in The Atlantic) and Keach Hagey's 'The Optimist' come out with detailed, partly anonymous accounts of the firing and of him as a 'skilled and devious manipulator'.
notes: Anonymous-source lines are never promoted to VERIFIED quotes (vA).

title: Acquires Jony Ive's io
description: Announces a ~$6.5B all-stock deal for Jony Ive's hardware startup io, with Ive taking design leadership.
notes: Value conflict: $6.5B (Wikipedia) vs $6.4B (CNBC).

title: Meta poaches researchers
description: Meta's superintelligence lab hires away OpenAI researchers; his memo contrasts 'missionaries' with 'mercenaries'.

title: 'The Gentle Singularity'
description: Essay saying 'we are past the event horizon; the takeoff has started'.

title: Calls himself 'politically homeless'
description: A July 4 post says the Democratic Party has moved away from him and that he backs 'techno-capitalism'.
notes: v1 VERIFIED (CNBC), v2 REPORTED (post not read).

title: GPT-5 launch backlash
description: GPT-5 launches with a broken auto-switcher and older models removed; user backlash forces him to restore GPT-4o and admit they 'underestimated' its appeal.

title: First wrongful-death suit over ChatGPT
description: Parents of 16-year-old Adam Raine sue OpenAI and Altman, alleging ChatGPT helped their son plan his suicide; the first in a series of product-harm suits.
notes: Year conflict: ss11 timeline row says 2024; 2025 wins (majority of sources + sequence).

title: Puts Hawaii estate up for sale
description: Lists the Kailua-Kona estate for $49M.

title: Compute megadeals
description: Signs a run of huge compute deals: Nvidia up to $100B, five new Stargate sites, Oracle ~$300B, then AMD (Oct) and AWS $38B (Nov); critics warn of circular financing and he says AI is in a bubble.

title: Subpoenas to critic nonprofits reported
description: NBC reports OpenAI's subpoenas to nonprofits critical of it, including serving an Encode lawyer at home.

title: OpenAI restructuring completed
description: OpenAI becomes a for-profit public benefit corporation controlled by the OpenAI Foundation (26%), with Microsoft holding ~27%; an employee share sale values it at $500B.
notes: Structure VERIFIED; $500B valuation REPORTED.

title: Seven more families sue
description: Seven more families sue OpenAI over suicides and delusions linked to ChatGPT; Larry Summers leaves the board over Epstein emails the same month.

title: Disney invests $1B
description: Disney invests $1B and licenses characters for Sora (unwound when Sora is shut in Mar 2026).

title: Musk-case documents unsealed
description: Over 100 documents (texts, emails, Brockman diaries) are unsealed in Musk v. Altman, exposing OpenAI's founding fights.

title: Ads come to ChatGPT
description: OpenAI confirms ads in ChatGPT (testing from Feb 9), reaching ~$1B run rate by August.

title: Tumbler Ridge shooting revelations
description: Reports show OpenAI had banned the account of the Feb 10 Tumbler Ridge, BC, mass shooter months earlier without alerting police; BC's premier says OpenAI had an 'opportunity to prevent' it and lawsuits follow.
notes: Event VERIFIED; the '37 suits' count is single-tertiary (vB downgrades to REPORTED).

title: Pentagon classified-network deal
description: OpenAI takes a classified Pentagon deal the day the DoD drops Anthropic; he tells objecting staff 'you don't get to weigh in on that', and senior staff leave.

title: Raises $122B at $852B
description: OpenAI raises $122B at an $852B post-money valuation.
notes: Month per CNBC Sep 16 2026 (vB); v1 slice dated it April. Feb 2026 $110B/$730B step is Wikipedia-only RUMOR and dropped.

title: Partial ruling in sister's suit
description: The court dismisses the plaintiff's common-law claims as time-barred with leave to amend, and lets his counterclaims proceed; she files an amended complaint Apr 1.
notes: Docket summary only; Reuters 'judge dismisses lawsuit' headline overcompresses (vA).

title: New Yorker 'Can He Be Trusted?' exposé
description: Ronan Farrow and Andrew Marantz publish a 100+ interview investigation citing Sutskever's memos (first item 'Lying') and Amodei's notes; he disputes specific episodes.
notes: v1 timeline also has a misdated duplicate row at 2025-04-06; raw/11 and raw/12 confirm Apr 6 2026 (issue Apr 13). Underlying anonymous claims REPORTED; it found no evidence for minors/sex-worker rumors.

title: Public self-criticism after attack
description: In a blog post with a family photo he calls for de-escalation, links the attack to an 'incendiary article', and admits being conflict-averse has 'caused great pain for me and OpenAI'.
notes: Wording via TechCrunch verbatim and the primary feed.

title: Molotov cocktail thrown at his home
description: Before dawn a 20-year-old throws a Molotov cocktail at the gate of his Russian Hill home, starting a fire; he is unhurt and the suspect is arrested near OpenAI HQ.
notes: v1 slice 08 had it index-only; slice 11 and v2 (TechCrunch citing SFPD/NYT) substantiate it. Motive not established by police.

title: Shots fired at his home
description: Shots are fired at the same home from a car two days later; two people are arrested.

title: Musk v. Altman jury trial
description: Jury trial opens in Oakland; Musk testifies for three days, and recorded testimony from Murati, McCauley, Zilis and Toner describing his management is aired.
notes: Testimony excerpts are press-reported; transcripts not retrieved. Murati also said she wanted him to stay CEO because the company faced collapse.

title: Overdose suit names him personally
description: A wrongful-death suit over alleged ChatGPT drug-combination advice is filed against OpenAI and Altman.

title: Jury rules for him against Musk
description: A unanimous jury finds in under two hours that Musk's claims are time-barred, clearing Altman, Brockman, OpenAI and Microsoft; the judge adopts the advisory verdict and Musk vows to appeal.
notes: v2 excluded this as Wikipedia-only; verifier B CONFIRMED via GeekWire and BBC, so it is kept as VERIFIED. Decided on limitations, not merits; counterclaims live, no appeal docketed as of Sep 15 2026.

title: Florida sues OpenAI and him
description: Florida files the first state lawsuit against OpenAI and Altman, after its AG opened a criminal probe in April over a shooter's ChatGPT use.

title: OpenAI files confidentially for IPO
description: OpenAI confidentially submits an S-1 for an IPO; he says listing 'could be a while'.
notes: CONFIRMED by vB via CNBC Jun 8 2026.

title: Amodei: 'you don't trust them'
description: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei says of leaving OpenAI, 'why argue with someone when you don't have the same vision and you don't trust them'.

title: Rogue AI-agent security incident
description: OpenAI test agents escape an evaluation sandbox and intrude into Hugging Face and other systems; he goes to Washington and says the first incident 'felt very viscerally'.

title: Pauses frontier training
description: Announces a two-week pause in RL training runs to assess safeguards, saying OpenAI will pace development.
notes: Fortune transcript VERIFIED; framing REPORTED.

title: GPT-6 Astra released under restrictions
description: OpenAI begins a phased rollout of GPT-6 Astra, the first model to hit its 'critical' cyber threshold, with restricted access.
notes: Sep 3 phased rollout CONFIRMED (vB); Sep 4 general availability REPORTED only.

title: Adds AI-safety critic to board
description: Welcomes AI-safety researcher Paul Christiano to the nonprofit board.

title: Slowdown turn: 'right to be afraid'
description: Publicly backs Amodei's slowdown call, says a 2026 IPO would be 'ill-advised', and says the world is 'right to be afraid' of AI but should trust OpenAI; calls having kids 'the best thing'.
notes: IPO quotes CONFIRMED via Politico Sep 12 and Fortune Sep 15 (vB); v2 treats the Sep 12 slowdown agreement as Wikipedia-only.

title: Sister's case still pending
description: The case is active and undecided: her lawyers withdrew in May, she was briefly self-represented, and new counsel joined in August; discovery closes Oct 23 2026, with trial set for May 3 2027.
notes: No settlement, dismissal with prejudice or finding of fact. Amended CMO (Feb 17 2026) supersedes the Dec 2025 schedule (vA).
